hypotheses.justification: The conclusion never mentions `hzw`; the hypothesis is only used inside the proof (in the step computing `hz : v' z = lookup xs 1`, whose `simp` needs `z ≠ w`). The statement is nevertheless provable without it. Split on `z = w`. In the `z ≠ w` branch the given proof applies verbatim. In the `z = w` branch, after `subst`, the conclusion is `Wff.Valid S (synWex y (.all z (.all z (synWb (classMem (opk (sn z) (sn z)) y) (classMem (opk z z) x)))))`. Since `Wff.Holds S v (.all z P) = ∀ a, Holds (update v z a) P`, the two nested `all z` collapse (`Holds v (.all z (.all z P)) ↔ ∀ b, Holds (update v z b) P`), so the goal is exactly the *diagonal* instance `∀ Z, ({Z},{Z}) ∈ Y ↔ (Z,Z) ∈ v x`. The witness `Y` obtained from `literalAxSi` at `v x` (`hY` satisfies `∀ Z W, ({Z},{W}) ∈ Y ↔ (Z,W) ∈ x`) satisfies this by taking `Z = W`; concretely, after `intro Z W` use `hY W W` and `DVec.cons W (DVec.cons W (DVec.cons Y (DVec.cons (v x) DVec.nil)))`, and the same `calc` goes through with `holds_literalSingletonPairMem hExt v' xs z z y 1 0 2` (both needed entries of `xs` equal `W`, `v' z = W` because `z` is updated last) and `holds_literalPairMem hExt v' xs z z x 1 0 3` (using `hyz`, `hxz`, `hxy`, which are still present). So `hzw` can be deleted; the other five distinctness hypotheses are still needed in this branch.

The statement does not need `x ≠ y`. Split on `x = y`. In the `x ≠ y` branch the given proof applies. In the `x = y` branch the conclusion is `Wff.Valid S (synWex y (.all z (.all w (synWb (classMem A (.cv y)) (classMem B (.cv y))))))` (`A = opk (sn z) (sn w)`, `B = opk z w`): both sides of the biconditional are `classMem` whose last argument is the existentially bound variable. Take the witness `Y := ∅`. Since `Wff.Holds S v (.classMem A (.cv y))` unfolds (SemanticCore.Basic, `Wff.Holds`, and `Class.Holds (.cv x) a = Mem S a (v x)`) to `∃ a, (∀ z, Mem S z a ↔ Class.Holds S v A z) ∧ Mem S a (v y)`, and likewise on the right, both sides become `∃ a, … ∧ Mem S a ∅`, hence both are false (`not_mem_emptyObj`), so the biconditional holds for every `Z`, `W`. An empty set exists under exactly the hypothesis `hNF`: `NFStandard/Equivalence.lean` gives `Fol.allRealizeSentence S NF ↔ Fol.allRealizeSentence S LiteralHailperinNF`, so stratified comprehension (`nf_comprehension`, `mem_comprehensionSet` in NFStandard/Basic) applies; alternatively `NFStandard/HailperinCylinder.lean` provides `emptyObj hH` and `not_mem_emptyObj hH` for `hH : Fol.allRealizeSentence S LiteralHailperinNF` (importable here without a cycle). So `hxy` can be deleted. The two deletions are independent: if both `x = y` and `z = w`, the formula becomes `∃Y ∀Z, ({Z},{Z}) ∈ Y ↔ (Z,Z) ∈ Y`, which again holds with `Y = ∅`.
